doc.title: Ray Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, AZ, April 16, 2000

title: Meeting Dizzy Gillespie through Hank Jones and the Snookum Russell background
summary: Hank Jones introduces Brown to Dizzy, who offers him a job; Brown explains his earlier time with Snookum Russell in the South and the three band offers he had sent for.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah. And at intermission at that club it was a singer named Billy Daniels and the guy playing piano for him was a guy that I knew called Hank Jones, who is one of the premier pianists even right as I speak. And Hank and I had lived in the YMCA up in Buffalo years before, when I first left home, my first job. And so I said to my cousin, “Come on, let’s go in there, I’m going to see if I can find Hank because I know him.” And so I walked back and he was in the back and we talked for a few minutes and he said, “Sit down” and we sat at an empty table. And we’re talking about what we had been doing since we hadn’t seen each other and he looked up and he said, “Oh there’s Dizzy Gillespie coming through the door.” I said, “Wow” I said, “introduce me to him, I want to meet him.” So Dizzy came in and he said, “Hey Diz,” Diz walked over. He said, “I want you to meet a friend of mine.” He said, “The kid’s a bass player, just got in town.” Dizzy looked at me and he said, “Yeah how are you” he said, “can you play?” And I said — you know what are you going to say when somebody asks you that? I looked at him — so Hank said, “Yeah he’s a great player.” So Dizzy said to me, “You want a job?” And I said, “Yeah.” So he gave me a card out of his pocket and said, “Be at my house tomorrow at seven P.M.” And I had already gotten a job, I had three job offers with three bands that I had sent away. I was in the south with a band called Snookum Russell, and they used to feature me all the time, because he and I used to do that Blanton-Ellington stuff, and we used to do that stuff that Slam and Lester Young did, because there was a guy that played like Lester Young in the band. And so they used to have flyers out, only in the south see, saying the Snookum Russell Orchestra featuring Ray Brown, world’s greatest bass player. This was when I was eighteen years old, the biggest lie ever. But you know, nobody would know down in Mississippi so they didn’t care. But I was trying to get out of the South and out of all of the stuff that was going on down there, I don’t have to talk about. So I sent flyers to, I was reading a DownBeat magazine, and I sent flyers to two or three agencies and then I waited about three weeks and I called my mother and I said, “Did you hear from anybody?” She said, “Yeah, you got offers from Lucky Millinder’s band, Andy Kirk’s band and some other band. So she said, “Which one are you going to take?” I said, “I don’t know I’ll wait ‘till I get to New York and find out.” And so now © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-
